title: An airfield burning, photographed from the air
researchNotes: Identified by Larry 2026-08-23 (giscus-vn-0074-c18118935): "This is a B-50 Canberra bomber on fire. Two of these got blown up in Bien Hoa." The Canberra flown in Vietnam was the B-57; the B-50 is a different aircraft. His words stand as given; the type number is recorded as a soft detail. Which event he means, and when, is his to say first (the guide asks him to date it himself), so the candidate event and its date are kept out of this record (research/photos/held-from-records-2026-09-14.md). Nothing in the frame itself names the airfield. Description written from the scan before consulting the survey: the frame shows the fire from the air across a whole airfield, not an aircraft in close-up, so Larry is naming what he understood to be burning rather than what the photograph itself shows. The aerial vantage is itself evidence — he was airborne when he took it, consistent with the helicopter travel he describes.
description: An aerial photograph looking down on a large airfield from considerable height. A single intense orange fireball burns at ground level near the centre-left, throwing a dense black smoke column straight up before it leans and spreads into a grey pall across the upper left of the frame. Below, a long pale runway and taxiway run diagonally across the field, with dispersal areas, regular blocks of buildings and tent lines, and roads cut through red-brown bare earth. A densely built settlement occupies the right of the frame, and low hills show faintly through haze on the horizon. The image is a colour slide, its mount visible around the edges.
